A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LPOSS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LPOSS and LPOSS+ segmentation results, ablations, sensitivity analyses and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds LPOSS and LPOSS+ evaluations on the MESS benchmark.

M1.justification: Patch-level label propagation, prediction jointly across windows and pixel-level refinement remain unchanged. The MESS experiments use backbone and window-ensemble variants already present in v1.

E1.justification: Section 8.4 and Tables 7–8 add evaluations on 22 MESS datasets spanning General, Earth Monitoring, Medical Sciences, Engineering and Biology. This substantially broadens represented domains beyond the eight retained segmentation benchmarks.

E2.justification: CAT-Seg is added as an evaluated comparator in the new MESS experiments. This is a focused addition of one segmentation-trained comparator; comparator membership in the existing experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The MESS evaluation introduces domain-level and Non-general dataset averages alongside per-dataset mIoU. Tables 7–8 specify backbone and window configurations for this comparison. Previously reported evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 8.4 adds a domain-generalization study comparing performance across domains described as close to or distant from CAT-Seg's training distribution. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter studies, window analyses and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests. No repeated-run counts, seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results, while Tables 7–8 add substantial domain-level and per-dataset MESS results. For example, LPOSS+ with DINO ViT-B/16 and 224×224 windows reports 41.8 Medical Sciences and 28.8 Engineering mIoU, versus CAT-Seg's 32.3 and 20.5. These are new comparisons under the stated method-specific settings, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores.

T1.justification: Equation (5) makes the existing degree normalization explicit using node-specific square-root degree denominators. This clarifies notation for the same quadratic objective; the mathematical reasoning, assumptions and LP solution remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a claim of outperforming pixel-level VLM fine-tuning approaches when test and training distributions differ substantially. The original contributions concerning training-free propagation, joint image prediction and pixel refinement remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 8.4 newly interprets medical and engineering advantages as evidence of better transfer beyond CAT-Seg's training distribution. It acknowledges CAT-Seg's General-domain advantage and attributes its Earth Monitoring advantage to higher image resolution and small-object segmentation.

D1.justification: The new MESS captions document VLM/VM backbones, window sizes, ensemble composition and CAT-Seg's absence of sliding windows. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, code links and hardware/timing information are retained; Section 9's timing discussion is relocated rather than removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MESS, CAT-Seg and Ypsilantis and Chum's co-segmentation work. It extends positioning to generalization relative to segmentation-trained methods while retaining the established related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Short additions appear in the introduction, related work and results, together with the new supplementary Section 8.4. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged, with a localized clarification of Equation (5).

P2.justification: v2 adds domain-summary Table 7 and dataset-level Table 8. Existing Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–6 are retained, with localized reflow and repositioning of appendix tables and text rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The MESS evaluation improves evidence about applicability beyond the original benchmarks, exposing both advantages and disadvantages against CAT-Seg through domain and dataset breakdowns. The gain is qualified: one added trained comparator and differing input resolutions do not fully substantiate the introduction's broader fine-tuning generalization claim. The core method and original experimental support remain intact.
